QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_33

question.text: Under SEBI's Code of Conduct for Investment Managers, a Manager who commits to transactions on behalf of the Fund must:

answer.text: Share all deal details with competing AIFs
Document all relevant correspondence and understanding during a deal with counterparties as per the records of the AIF

explanation.text: The Logic: Per clause (l) of the Code of Conduct in Chapter 11.6: Managers shall document all relevant correspondence and understanding during a deal with counterparties as per the records of the AIF, if they have committed to transactions on behalf of the Fund. The Trap: Destroying correspondence, sharing with competitors and relying on oral commitments all directly contradict the Code (clauses on record-keeping, confidentiality and due-diligence). Cross-Exam Context: Same clause in XIX-C/D. Also anchors the 'record in writing' duty for investment decisions. Manager's Pro-Tip: Use a deal-room SaaS (e.g., with MOA/NDA tracking) so every piece of deal correspondence is automatically archived with counterparty identity and timestamp — this is your first line of defence if a counterparty later disputes pricing or indicative terms.
